newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn, soybeans post good progress.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn, soybeans post good progress.

text.p: Corn and soybean development progressed well during the week ended Sunday with a few areas of the state receiving rain but pockets of dryness were showing up, according to the Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service.
As of Sunday, the corn crop was rated 70 percent good to excellent, the same as the previous week. Twenty-four percent of the crop was fair, five percent poor and one percent very poor.

Soybean planting was virtually complete and 70 percent of the crop was good to excellent, above the 65 percent in that category the previous week. Twenty-five percent of the crop was fair, four percent poor and one percent very poor.
Wheat harvest was 45 percent complete compared with 57 percent a year ago and 57 percent average.

Topsoil moisture was five percent surplus, 71 percent adequate, 21 percent short and three percent very short. Subsoil moisture levels were four percent surplus, 83 percent adequate, 12 percent short and one percent very short.

Subsoil moisture levels were four percent surplus, 83 percent adequate, 12 percent short and one percent very short. Pasture conditions were 10 percent excellent, 55 percent good, 28 percent fair, six percent poor and one percent very poor.
